question: A 56-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of pain and swelling in his left leg. He has a history of pancreatic cancer and is currently receiving chemotherapy. Three weeks ago, he had a similar episode in his right arm that resolved without treatment. His temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F). Palpation of the left leg shows a tender, cord-shaped structure medial to the medial condyle of the femur. The overlying skin is erythematous. Which of the following vessels is most likely affected?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Pancreatic cancer -> increased risk of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) -> chemotherapy-induced hypercoagulability -> 80% CHAIN: Pain and swelling in left leg -> palpable cord-shaped structure -> erythematous skin -> signs of thrombophlebitis -> 70% CHAIN: Tender cord-shaped structure medial to medial condyle of femur -> likely thrombosed vein -> possible deep femoral vein involvement -> 60% CHAIN: History of similar episode in right arm -> resolved without treatment -> possible superficial thrombophlebitis -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with pain, swelling, tenderness, and erythema in the left leg, along with a cord-shaped structure, is suggestive of deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Given the location described, the most likely affected vessel is the deep femoral vein.
